description: Bean-and-pasta soup that lands in half an hour. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

ingredients.name: Parmesan Cheese
ingredients.notes: finely grated, plus rind if you have it

steps.title: Bloom aromatics in olive oil
steps.instruction: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or stockpot over medium. Cook onion with a pinch of salt until softened and lightly golden at the edges, 6–8 minutes. Stir in garlic and tomato paste; cook until the paste darkens and smells sweet, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer broth and beans
steps.instruction: Add kidney beans, broth, oregano, bay leaves, and Parmesan rind if using. Bring to a steady simmer — the soup should look brothy, not stew-thick yet. Simmer 10 minutes so flavors meld and beans heat through.

steps.title: Cook pasta in the soup
steps.instruction: Stir in ditalini and simmer until pasta is tender with a little bite, 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally so pasta does not stick. The consistency should coat a spoon lightly — add a splash of water if it tightens too much before service.

steps.title: Finish and season the pot
steps.instruction: Fish out bay leaves and rind. Stir in half the grated Parmesan off heat until melted. Taste and adjust salt and pepper — the soup should be savory and tomato-forward, not bland brothy.

steps.title: Ladle and garnish at the line
steps.instruction: Ladle into bowls. Pass parsley and remaining Parmesan separately so greens stay bright. Serve bread on the side. Hold the pot on the lowest simmer up to 45 minutes; add broth if pasta swells — stir before each ladle.

proTips: Assign one cook to proteins and one to sides — rookies stay on timing, not multitasking.
Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate 30-Minute Pasta e Fagioli for the Hall with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up 30-Minute Pasta e Fagioli for the Hall on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Bean-and-pasta soup that lands in half an hour. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
